khon-ninh-cung: A brand-new painting of a natural, lived-in, richly furnished room, painted exactly like image 1 (the bedroom): same hand, same brushwork, same soft painterly finish, same natural warm colours, saturation and contrast, same depth with furniture, curtains and objects arranged through the whole room from the foreground to the back. Wide panoramic, eye-level view, summer morning. ROOM: Khôn Ninh cung main reception hall, where the Empress of an ancient Chinese imperial palace receives the consorts, a real room in daily use, no bed anywhere: a GRAND, very large and high hall (owner Lượt 563: never a small room), seen straight on along its central axis, with the back wall straight across the picture and both side walls running towards the viewer in correct perspective, meeting the back wall at square corners; red lacquer columns wrapped with gilded phoenix carving stand in two straight rows along the hall; a high coffered ceiling painted gold and red; a large horizontal gilt plaque carved with phoenixes and clouds (no writing, no characters) high on the back wall, centred; a carved gilded openwork floor-to-ceiling arch frame (a luozhao) spans the whole width of the hall from wall to wall, square to the back wall, carved with phoenixes among peonies, framing the raised throne area behind it; inside it, on a wide platform of three steps with a gilded balustrade, against the back wall, exactly centred and seen straight on, the Empress's throne: a wide gilded carved throne seat with a tall carved panel back crowned by a golden phoenix, imperial yellow silk cushions embroidered with phoenixes, a small low table with a gold tea set beside it on the platform; behind the throne a large five-panel gilded screen with a phoenix among peonies; on each side of the throne a tall ceremonial fan of imperial yellow silk with a phoenix on a long gilded pole, and a pair of golden phoenix figures on tall stands; in front of the arch frame, at the foot of the platform, a gold crane-shaped incense burner on each side; TWO straight rows of carved gilded square-backed armchairs with imperial yellow cushions and small tea tables between them (owner Lượt 563), one row along each side wall, mirrored exactly on the central axis, the two rows facing each other across the open central aisle that leads to the throne platform, each chair lined up with the columns and square to the walls, the rows starting from the arch frame and ending half way towards the viewer; NO table and NO stools in the middle of the floor (owner Lượt 554): the central aisle in front of the platform stays open for people to stand; imperial yellow silk curtains tied back with gold tassels at the windows of the side walls, golden lattice windows onto a sunny summer garden, ornate gilded palace lanterns with yellow tassels hanging in pairs, cloisonné vases of peonies, gilded curio shelves of jade and gold treasures against the side walls behind the chairs. The most dazzling room of the whole palace: imperial yellow silk and gold everywhere, phoenix motifs carved, embroidered and gilded, red lacquer pillars wrapped with gold, the richest treasures. No Western sofa, no upholstered couch. ROOM SHAPE (owner Lượt 491): the room reads rectilinear with square corners, straight walls and straight beams, never a curved hall, never furniture in an arc or a curve; every piece of furniture stands in clear straight lines along the walls, square to the walls, orderly, never scattered and never at a slant. LAYOUT NUMBERS (owner Lượt 477, 520): seen as close and as low as in image 3 (image 3 is only a guide for how close, how rich and how finely made the room is, NOT for its arrangement, colours or furniture: this hall has its own different, grander arrangement as written above); the main throne platform is large and clear, its base at about two thirds of the picture height; the chair rows come down to about seven eighths of the picture height; the open floor of the central aisle in front is only a strip of about one tenth of the picture height at the bottom, and nothing stands on it, because people will stand there. FLOOR: polished stone tiles visible between the furniture, no large rug or carpet covering the floor (at most a small mat under the platform steps); the throne platform sits in the central half of the width. LIGHT: soft warm morning daylight from the right, like the light on the girl in image 2, so a person standing in the room looks lit by it. Do not leave the room empty like a stage; it should feel natural and furnished, people will simply be placed in it later. LEFT SIDE (owner Lượt 406): the left part of the room near the viewer stays open like in image 1 — only small, low objects there at most, never a large piece of furniture or a big object close up at the left edge, because people will stand on the left. Empty of people, no text.

Wide panoramic, eye-level view, summer morning. ROOM: Trường Xuân cung chính điện bedroom, the private bedchamber of the Imperial Noble Consort (Hoàng quý phi), the highest consort below the Empress, in ancient China, a real room in daily use, seen straight on with the back wall straight across the picture and the right side wall running towards the viewer in clear perspective, meeting at a square corner; dark zitan pillars and beams with gold lacquer; the main subject is a grand walk-in canopy bed (a babu bed: a bed built like a small carved room with its own front porch and a carved openwork front gate) standing against the back wall, centred, square to it and seen straight on, the large clear main subject, its carved front gate open, golden yellow silk curtains lined with ruby red tied back inside, golden yellow brocade bedding embroidered with white magnolias and a pair of small phoenixes, pearl strings on the gate; to the left of the bed, flat against the back wall, a tall folding screen with kingfisher-blue feather inlay and magnolias; to the right of the bed a carved openwork partition with a tall vase-shaped doorway giving a glimpse of a dressing room; tall carved lattice windows in the right side wall onto a sunny courtyard garden with a magnolia tree; along the walls a gold-lacquer dressing table with a tall bronze mirror and a jewellery cabinet open with pearls and jade, a zitan curio shelf of jade, coral and cloisonné treasures, ornate hanging palace lanterns with ruby red tassels, a clothes stand with a ruby red robe, cloisonné vases of magnolia branches, a gold incense burner, slippers on the bed porch step. Trường Xuân cung signature style, the same in every room of this palace: white magnolias (ngọc lan) are its flower, painted on the screens, embroidered on the silks and in the vases; borders of the endless swastika fret and round longevity medallions carved in the beams and furniture; dark zitan sandalwood with gold lacquer and mother-of-pearl inlay; square-backed zitan furniture (never round-backed); a tall vase-shaped doorway (never a round moon gate) in a carved openwork partition; screens with kingfisher-blue feather inlay. HOÀNG QUÝ PHI level, the Vice-Empress (phó hậu, owner Lượt 572): nearly as splendid as the Empress, only one small step below her: rich gilt carving everywhere on the furniture, gold lacquer, mother-of-pearl, pearls, jade, coral, cloisonné and kingfisher-blue inlay, many treasures; the main seats and the bed look imperial and throne-like, with tall carved gilded backs and gilded frames, close to the Empress's own.  COLOURS (owner Lượt 572): golden yellow is strong and clearly visible, about HALF as much yellow as in the Empress's room: golden yellow silk curtains and bed curtains, golden yellow brocade bedding, seat brocades and cushions, mixed with deep ruby red silks, lanterns and tassels and with dark zitan and red lacquer wood, so the room reads golden and imperial, only a little less yellow than the Empress's room. Phoenixes allowed: a pair of phoenixes carved and gilded or embroidered among magnolias on the bed, the screen and the cushions, and a pair of small gilded phoenix figures. ROOM SHAPE (owner Lượt 491): the room reads rectilinear with square corners, straight walls and straight beams, never a curved hall, never furniture in an arc or a curve; every piece of furniture stands in clear straight lines along the walls, square to the walls, orderly, never scattered and never at a slant. Keep the same room and the same arrangement as image 3 (this same room as drawn before): the same walls, windows, furniture places and the same distance; change only the colours and the richness as written here. The right corner is furnished, never empty or bare: a table group stands there inside the outer fifth of the width, set back from the bottom edge, between one half and seven eighths of the picture height, so a person standing in front of it covers it naturally. FLOOR: warm polished wooden floorboards visible between the furniture, no large rug or carpet covering the floor (at most a small mat under the bed porch step); the walk-in canopy bed sits in the central half of the width. LIGHT: soft warm morning daylight from the right, like the light on the girl in image 2, so a person standing in the room looks lit by it.
